'''Tyrese Kendrid Maxey''' (born November 4, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is known for his elite speed, dribbling, and shot-making.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carlin |first=Ky |last2=read |first2=Sixers Wire·1 min |date=2026-06-20 |title=Top 100 NBA player ranking revealed for Sixers star Tyrese Maxey |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/top-100-nba-player-ranking-144416595.html |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]].

Born in [[Dallas]], Texas, Maxey was a [[shooting guard]] for [[South Garland High School]], helping the team to their first-ever Texas state high school basketball tournament appearance in 2018. A [[College recruiting|five-star recruit]] as early as his sophomore year of high school, Maxey contemplated leaving high school early to play for the Kentucky Wildcats, but ultimately stayed at South Garland, where he was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and [[Texas Mr. Basketball]] during his senior year. He then played for the Wildcats, where he would set a school record of 26 [[Point (basketball)|points]] in his collegiate debut.

After Maxey's freshman season at Kentucky was interrupted by the [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports|COVID-19 pandemic]], he elected to enter the [[2020 NBA draft]], where the 76ers selected him 21st overall with their first-round pick. Maxey received limited playing time during his rookie season, making his first NBA [[starting lineup|start]] in a game where the 76ers could only field the league's minimum number of players. However, [[Ben Simmons]]'s refusal to play for the 76ers the following season gave Maxey an opportunity to become the team's starting [[point guard]]. In his fourth season, Maxey won the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player Award]] and earned his first [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] selection in 2024.

====2023–24 season: First All-Star selection and Most Improved Player====
On November 12, 2023, Maxey put up a then career-high 50 points along with seven rebounds, five assists, and three blocks in a 137–126 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/sixers-vs-pacers-instant-breakdown-joel-embiid-tyrese-haliburton|title=Sixers-Pacers instant breakdown: Tyrese Maxey goes off on career-high night|website=ClutchPoints|last=DiGiovanni|first=Sam|date=November 12, 2023|access-date=November 12, 2023}}</ref> He became the sixth Sixer ever with 50+ points, 5+ rebounds and 5+ assists ([[Allen Iverson]], [[Joel Embiid]], [[Wilt Chamberlain]], [[Hal Greer]] and [[Dana Barros]]). Maxey also joined Iverson as the only Sixers with 50+ points at 23 or younger.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Starting 5, Nov. 13: Iverson and Maxey have this in common now |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-starting-5-nov-13 |access-date=13 November 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> He also dedicated his career-high to his teammate [[Kelly Oubre Jr.]], who was struck by a car by a [[hit and run]] driver and went to the hospital the previous day.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/11/13/76ers-tyrese-maxey-dedicates-first-ever-50-point-game-to-kelly-oubre |title=76ers' Tyrese Maxey Dedicates First-Ever 50-Point Game to Kelly Oubre |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=18 November 2023}}</ref> On December 29, Maxey scored 42 points in a 131–127 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tyrese Maxey scores 42 points, short-handed 76ers outlast Rockets 131-127 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585062|access-date=31 December 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On February 1, 2024, Maxey was named to his first career [[2024 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] as an Eastern Conference reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 NBA All-Star reserves announced |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2024-nba-all-star-reserves-announced |access-date=2024-02-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> On the same day, Maxey scored a then career-high 51 points in a 127–124 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/76ers-vs-jazz-instant-breakdown-tyrese-maxey|title=76ers vs. Jazz instant breakdown: Tyrese Maxey scores career-high 51 in return|website=ClutchPoints|last=DiGiovanni|first=Sam|date=February 1, 2024|access-date=February 1, 2024}}</ref> On April 4, Maxey fell one rebound short of a first career triple double, putting up 37 points, 11 assists in an important win at the [[Miami Heat]]. On April 7, Maxey scored a career-high 52 points in a 133–126 double–overtime win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/76ers-vs-spurs-instant-breakdown-tyrese-maxey-victor-wembanyama|title=76ers vs. Spurs instant breakdown: Tyrese Maxey takes over in wild 2OT win|website=ClutchPoints|last=DiGiovanni|first=Sam|date=April 7, 2024|access-date=April 7, 2024}}</ref> Maxey finished his 4th season with the 76ers averaging 25.9 points per game and 6.2 assists per game. Maxey finished the season as one of three players to put up 3 or more 50 point games during the season, a list including teammate Joel Embiid and [[Phoenix Suns]] shooting guard [[Devin Booker]].

On April 23, 2024, Maxey was named the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24]] [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]], winning over [[Coby White]] and [[Alperen Şengün]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chiari |first=Mike |date=April 23, 2024 |title=76ers' Tyrese Maxey Wins 2023–24 NBA Most Improved Player of the Year Award |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10116715-76ers-tyrese-maxey-wins-2023-24-nba-most-improved-player-of-the-year-award |access-date=April 23, 2024 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> On April 30, Maxey put up a playoff career-high 46 points in the Sixers' 112–106 victory in Game 5 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs#(2) New York Knicks vs. (7) Philadelphia 76ers|first round of the playoffs]] against the [[New York Knicks]]. He scored 7 straight points in the last 25 seconds of regulation to tie the game after being down 96–90, including a 34-foot, game-tying shot with 8.1 seconds left.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/76ers-news-tyrese-maxey-hail-mary-force-overtime-knicks-fans-in-shock|title=Tyrese Maxey's Hail Mary to force overtime vs Knicks has 76ers fans in utter shock|website=ClutchPoints|last=Sampson|first=Peter|date=April 30, 2024|access-date=April 30, 2024}}</ref> The 76ers eventually lost the series in 6 games. ==Personal life==
[[File:Council President Clarke Joins 76er Tyrese Maxey for Toy Distribution at Richard Wright Elementary School 12-17-21 (51759976730).jpg|thumb|Maxey at a charity event for his foundation|alt=Maxey, wearing a red t-shirt over a gray hoodie and in a mask, leans over a podium.]]
Maxey is one of four children; he has three sisters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tyrese Maxey{{snd}}Men's Basketball |url=https://ukathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tyrese--maxey/7521 |work=Kentucky Wildcats |access-date=March 3, 2022 |archive-date=February 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220043430/https://ukathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tyrese--maxey/7521 |url-status=live }}</ref> During the 2017–18 college basketball season, their father Tyrone was the director of player development for Southern Methodist University, one of the schools that attempted to recruit his son.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Report: Father of 5-star basketball recruit Tyrese Maxey leaves his position at SMU |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2018/04/13/report-father-of-5-star-basketball-recruit-tyrese-maxey-leaves-his-position-at-smu/ |work=The Dallas Morning News |date=April 13, 2018 |access-date=March 3, 2022 |archive-date=March 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220303184456/https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2018/04/13/report-father-of-5-star-basketball-recruit-tyrese-maxey-leaves-his-position-at-smu/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During the NBA season, he lives in [[Voorhees Township, New Jersey]]. His Voorhees home caught fire on [[Christmas Eve]] in 2021, while his family was visiting for the holiday, but nobody was injured, and the 76ers provided Maxey with housing accommodations and other resources for him and his family.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mizell |first=Gina |title=Tyrese Maxey feels 'blessed' his family is OK after house fire |url=https://www.inquirer.com/sports/sixers-tyrese-maxey-fire-20211227.html |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=December 26, 2021 |access-date=March 3, 2022 |url-access=limited }}</ref>

Maxey is childhood friends with fellow NBA player [[R. J. Hampton]]. Although they played basketball in the same geographic region since first grade, they were never teammates, only opponents.<ref>{{cite news |last=Caplan |first=Callie |title=Before NBA draft, South Garland's Tyrese Maxey reflects on advice from LeBron James, friendship with RJ Hampton |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2020/11/16/before-nba-draft-south-garlands-tyrese-maxey-reflects-on-advice-from-lebron-james-friendship-with-rj-hampton/ |work=The Dallas Morning News |date=November 16, 2020 |access-date=March 3, 2022 |archive-date=March 1, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301110516/https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2020/11/16/before-nba-draft-south-garlands-tyrese-maxey-reflects-on-advice-from-lebron-james-friendship-with-rj-hampton/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He is also one of the "Baggage Claim Boys", a loose group of star high school basketball players from the [[Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex]] who became friends during their college recruiting season. The group also includes Timothy Leach, [[Isaac Likekele]] and [[Drew Timme]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Unruh |first=Jacob |title=OSU basketball: Isaac Likekele, Chris Harris Jr. are part of the Baggage Claim Boys |url=https://oklahoman.com/article/5652051/osu-basketball-isaac-likekele-chris-harris-jr-are-part-of-the-baggage-claim-boys |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |date=January 11, 2020 |access-date=March 3, 2022 |archive-date=October 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022154729/https://oklahoman.com/article/5652051/osu-basketball-isaac-likekele-chris-harris-jr-are-part-of-the-baggage-claim-boys |url-status=live |url-access=limited}}</ref>

Outside of basketball, Maxey is a devoted fan of [[Marvel Comics]] and the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Clancy |first=Shamus |title=Maxey is a superhero on the court and a comic book superfan off it |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/sixers-rookie-tyrese-maxey-marvel-comics-buff |work=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]] |date=November 20, 2020 |access-date=March 3, 2022 |archive-date=March 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304132111/https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/sixers-rookie-tyrese-maxey-marvel-comics-buff |url-status=live }}</ref> His favorite Marvel Cinematic Universe films include ''[[Spider-Man: Homecoming]]'' and ''[[The Avengers (2012 film)|The Avengers]]'', and he has previously compared himself to the character [[Spider-Man]].<ref name="slam" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hale |first=Jon |title=Avengers assemble! Tyrese Maxey compares UK teammates to Marvel heroes |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2019/09/25/kentucky-basketball-which-avengers-marvel-hero-would-each-player-be/2411234001/ |work=The Courier-Journal |date=September 25, 2019 |access-date=March 3, 2022 |url-access=limited |archive-date=March 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220303184445/https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2019/09/25/kentucky-basketball-which-avengers-marvel-hero-would-each-player-be/2411234001/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He also runs a [[charitable foundation]], the Tyrese Maxey Foundation, which has partnered with Youth Services, Inc., to help prevent [[truancy]] in Philadelphia-area schools.<ref>{{cite news |last=Pompey |first=Keith |title=Sixers star Tyrese Maxey partnered with a Philly youth program to reward local students |url=https://www.inquirer.com/sports/sixers-tyrese-maxey-partners-with-ysi-20211126.html |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=November 26, 2021 |access-date=March 3, 2022 |url-access=limited |archive-date=January 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220131053031/https://www.inquirer.com/sports/sixers-tyrese-maxey-partners-with-ysi-20211126.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>https://thesixersense.com/insider-reveals-tyrese-maxey-plot-that-76ers-fans-knew-since-last-season-01kbgftxadtg</ref>
